This exactly establishes the missing-trigger obligation from the closed source facts alone, independent of any predicate execution (plan/receipt show predicate_id=null and backend=none, which is a W-boundary unavailability, not evidence against the semantic finding). The dossier's own strongest_rebuttal states that 'the closed model is consistent with itself; the divergence is between the author text and the declaration semantics that produced the model' — this is not a competent alternative reading of the transition's own trigger semantics, it merely observes that the model was authored to diverge from the NL text, which does not rebut but rather concedes the missing-trigger fact. Because this offered rebuttal does not supply any exact fact establishing that the transition does carry a trigger, or that the guard-only form is equivalent to a trigger in this closed model, the alleged rebuttal is defeated by the explicit UML completion-transition rule and the exact absence of any trigger token in the source line.

semantic_adjudication.basis: candidate and binding fields of dossier for 0054:r1:i8 (PlantUML source line 15 'InMotion --> EmergencyStopping : [obstacle detected]'; UML 2.5.1 §14.2.3.8.3 completion-transition semantics cited in candidate.reason); predicate/backend fields noting predicate_id=null/backend=none are W-boundary facts only, not used as D evidence
semantic_adjudication.reason: The closed PlantUML source at line 15 declares `InMotion --> EmergencyStopping : [obstacle detected]`, i.e., only a bracketed guard token with no trigger name before the bracket. Per UML 2.5.1 §14.2.3.8.3, a transition with no trigger is a completion transition, fired only upon completion of internal activity in the source state; InMotion (state:InMotion:line:8) is a simple, non-activity composite state in the closed model, so this transition can never fire under the completion-transition semantics the model itself encodes. This exactly establishes the missing-trigger obligation from the closed source facts alone, independent of any predicate execution (plan/receipt show predicate_id=null and backend=none, which is a W-boundary unavailability, not evidence against the semantic finding). The dossier's own strongest_rebuttal states that 'the closed model is consistent with itself; the divergence is between the author text and the declaration semantics that produced the model' — this is not a competent alternative reading of the transition's own trigger semantics, it merely observes that the model was authored to diverge from the NL text, which does not rebut but rather concedes the missing-trigger fact. Because this offered rebuttal does not supply any exact fact establishing that the transition does carry a trigger, or that the guard-only form is equivalent to a trigger in this closed model, the alleged rebuttal is defeated by the explicit UML completion-transition rule and the exact absence of any trigger token in the source line.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The divergence between the author's NL requirement (naming an 'obstacle detected' trigger) and the model's actual bracket-only guard declaration reflects an authoring inconsistency between text and model, not a genuine alternative reading of the transition's own trigger semantics; the closed model, read on its own UML completion-transition terms, still lacks any trigger for InMotion -> EmergencyStopping.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The transition from InMotion to EmergencyStopping must be triggered by an event named 'obstacle detected' as required by the governing NL requirement; a bracketed guard alone does not constitute a trigger.

decisions.reason: NL9 describes two behavioral clauses for Approaching: sending the Send signal and continuing to approach the destination. The closed FCSTM exposes exactly one abstract 'during' action (Send) attached to Approaching's do-phase slot (state:Approaching:line:13), and the S4 backend receipt confirms no distinct action literally named 'approach the destination' is attached to that lifecycle slot (verdict=false). This establishes the candidate's exact semantic gap: no independently confirmable second do-phase carrier exists. However, pyfcstm's during/do slot is architecturally the single carrier for all continuous behavior of a state, so the same abstract 'during Send' action is a competent reading that folds both the signal-emission and destination-approach semantics into one carrier, exactly as the model's author apparently intended by giving Approaching only one do-phase action. This is the strongest_rebuttal already identified in the dossier: 'the single during abstract Send carrier could be read as encompassing both the send action and the continuous approach activity, since pyfcstm's during/do slot models continuous behavior.' This rebuttal is supported by the exact binding fact that Approaching has one and only one do-phase carrier in the closed model, so it survives as a competent alternative reading rather than being excluded by any exact contrary fact.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The single 'during abstract Send' carrier attached to Approaching's do-phase slot could be read as encompassing both the send action and the continuous approach-to-destination activity, since pyfcstm's during/do slot models all continuous behavior of a state as one carrier; under this reading NL9-ACTION-2 is satisfied by the same carrier that satisfies NL9-ACTION-1, and no separate ongoing-progress carrier is required.
decisions.violated_obligation: State Approaching must continuously perform an approach-to-destination activity while active (a do-phase continuous behavior), per NL-CONTRACT-NL9-ACTION-2 and NL9's clause 'and continues to approach the destination'.

decisions.basis: candidate and binding fields of dossier for 0054:r1:i8 (PlantUML source line 15 'InMotion --> EmergencyStopping : [obstacle detected]'; UML 2.5.1 §14.2.3.8.3 completion-transition semantics cited in candidate.reason); predicate/backend fields noting predicate_id=null/backend=none are W-boundary facts only, not used as D evidence
decisions.reason: The closed PlantUML source at line 15 declares `InMotion --> EmergencyStopping : [obstacle detected]`, i.e., only a bracketed guard token with no trigger name before the bracket. Per UML 2.5.1 §14.2.3.8.3, a transition with no trigger is a completion transition, fired only upon completion of internal activity in the source state; InMotion (state:InMotion:line:8) is a simple, non-activity composite state in the closed model, so this transition can never fire under the completion-transition semantics the model itself encodes. This exactly establishes the missing-trigger obligation from the closed source facts alone, independent of any predicate execution (plan/receipt show predicate_id=null and backend=none, which is a W-boundary unavailability, not evidence against the semantic finding). The dossier's own strongest_rebuttal states that 'the closed model is consistent with itself; the divergence is between the author text and the declaration semantics that produced the model' — this is not a competent alternative reading of the transition's own trigger semantics, it merely observes that the model was authored to diverge from the NL text, which does not rebut but rather concedes the missing-trigger fact. Because this offered rebuttal does not supply any exact fact establishing that the transition does carry a trigger, or that the guard-only form is equivalent to a trigger in this closed model, the alleged rebuttal is defeated by the explicit UML completion-transition rule and the exact absence of any trigger token in the source line.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The divergence between the author's NL requirement (naming an 'obstacle detected' trigger) and the model's actual bracket-only guard declaration reflects an authoring inconsistency between text and model, not a genuine alternative reading of the transition's own trigger semantics; the closed model, read on its own UML completion-transition terms, still lacks any trigger for InMotion -> EmergencyStopping.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition from InMotion to EmergencyStopping must be triggered by an event named 'obstacle detected' as required by the governing NL requirement; a bracketed guard alone does not constitute a trigger.

All required transition endpoints and event-consumer sets are exactly present and reachable in the closed model per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts, so no wrong-target/consumer-coverage candidates are needed for endpoint/consumption contracts. State actions for EmergencyStopping (Emergency Stop, Obstacle Detected send) and Approaching (Send, continuous approach activity) map to abstract lifecycle carriers 'EmergencyStop', 'SendObstacleDetected', 'Send' with no do/entry-phase-triggered content beyond declaration; NL9-ACTION-2 (do-phase continuous activity / progress) and NL10-RETAIN-1 (state retention with guard condition) require behavioral evidence (progress/retention) that the closed model cannot certify beyond declaration, remaining precise W1 candidates. The Approaching/Cruising/Accelerating leaves route out via [*] with effect assignments to InMotion's own outgoing transitions gated by R45RouteToken, so InMotion-level continuation is real; but Stopping/EmergencyStopping have zero outgoing transitions and are leaves per LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostics -- these are declared endpoints (Stopping is not marked termination_state by NL) so I do not synthesize deadlock_freedom without an explicit progress obligation on those two states, consistent with the frontier discipline against inventing progress not requested by NL. No supplied contract asserts a termination_state role for Stopping/EmergencyStopping, so I refrain from termination-property invention. I focus produced candidates on the exact NL9/NL10 progress and retention obligations, which cannot be certified operationally by the closed deterministic facts (no trace/scenario evidence), keeping them W1 with predicate_id null, and on NL3 actions where lifecycle carriers exist but only as declared abstract actions without confirmed occurrence facts -- I omit those since the carrier is present (EmergencyStop, SendObstacleDetected exist as during actions on EmergencyStopping) and NL3-ACTION-1/2 are declaration-satisfied observations, not behavioral consequence gaps beyond what other lens covers. I emit no additional_contracts since no exact cross-view fact reveals an unseen causal defect distinct from already-supplied NL9/NL10 obligations.
